transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-06
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Product), Vikram Shah (ML), Rita Gomez (CTO), Tom Nguyen (Infra), Alex Park (Payments Ops)

Summary: Weekly POC sync for Orion Payments pilot. Reviewed benchmark progress, discussed tuning (batching, KV cache, quantization), clarified success criteria for business case closeout, and agreed on next steps for final benchmark and exec sign-off. Some minor transcription errors present.

00:00 - Maya Chen: hi everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, i think we're all set on time. quick roll call?
00:08 - Lena Ortiz: hey it's lena here, product.
00:10 - Vikram Shah: vikram, ml eng.
00:12 - Rita Gomez: rita, cto.
00:14 - Tom Nguyen: tom, infra.
00:16 - Alex Park: alex, payments ops.
00:18 - Samir Patel: samir from redwood, i'll lead the technical bits today.
00:22 - Maya Chen: cool, agenda — quick status on the POC metrics, samir will go deeper on tuning, then security/ops check and close with next steps.
00:34 - Samir Patel: thanks. ok so to start, we completed the 48 hour run on the hosted cluster with the anonymized sample set you sent last week. high level: throughput steady at ~180 qps for the end-to-end requests (note some request batching), p95 latency is 240ms, p99 around 480ms in the hosted config. we did a run with kv cache disabled first then enabled — with kv enabled p95 dropped ~25%. there was a transcription hiccup in the logs where "KV cache" printed as "k v cass" but it's fine.
01:05 - Vikram Shah: those numbers look close to what we saw in staging, though p99 480 is a bit higher than our target. our product goal was p95 <200ms and p99 <350ms, so we still have a gap.
01:18 - Samir Patel: understood. two levers we discussed: increase batch size and enable quantization/FP16 path for the model variant. on our dedicated variant we see p95 down to 160ms with same dataset in earlier benchmarks, but that was on a 8-gpu pool with persistent KV caching and optimized kernels. we can reproduce a similar config in private or dedicated.
01:42 - Tom Nguyen: ok can you remind us of the difference between the hosted test you ran and the dedicated setup? like network overhead etc.
01:48 - Samir Patel: sure — hosted runs on shared infra which can add jitter on tail latency; dedicated is reserved GPUs (no noisy neighbor), we also tune kernel selection and pre-warm KV caches. network egress is similar, but the infra route is shorter for dedicated inside our colo region. also we can provision larger batch windows without violating latency SLOs by adjusting the serving runtime.
02:10 - Lena Ortiz: how much of a cost delta is there? we need to make sure the business case still holds.
02:14 - Maya Chen: good question. early estimate: hosted run cost per 1M tokens processed was roughly $X (note: placeholder in call), dedicated committed sku cuts per-token price by ~35% at the volumes you're targeting. we'll send an updated pricing sheet after the final benchmark — that'll be concrete numbers.
02:34 - Alex Park: are you factoring in caching benefits? a lot of our traffic has repeated phrase patterns for refunds and chargebacks.
02:40 - Samir Patel: yes, prefix/KV caching is in scope — in fact we saw a 20-30% reduction in token compute for repeated prefixes in the run. for your workload where templates repeat, the effective cost per request drops more.
02:58 - Vikram Shah: on accuracy / quality: did enabling quantization affect classification accuracy for anomaly detection model? we can't have accuracy regressions >1.5% otherwise ops teams get anxious.
03:10 - Samir Patel: we ran a small eval set: INT8 quant produced negligible delta (~0.6% change) on top-line classification for your test set; FP16 was basically identical. caveat: that's on the inference-only evaluation; we recommend a 72-hour production-like run to validate drift and edge cases.
03:32 - Rita Gomez: from security side, we need SOC 2 type II evidence, SSO via SAML, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs. also data residency notes — payments data can't leave region. where are you with the private option?
03:48 - Maya Chen: we have a Private deployment option (VPC + on-prem connector). for SOC 2 and SAML we already have artifacts; i'll attach the security packet after the call. for KMS we support customer-managed keys and HSM in some regions. regarding residency, we can host in your preferred cloud region or run an on-prem appliance if needed.
04:10 - Tom Nguyen: great — to move to private we need to confirm VPC peering and firewall rules, plus IP ranges. i'll take that back.
04:18 - Samir Patel: also note a small gotcha: if you want on-prem we do a provisioning window — usually 2-3 weeks for access and certs. for a dedicated cloud pool we can spin up in ~5 days after SOW.
04:33 - Lena Ortiz: success criteria recap — can we read back what we have so exec alignment is clean?
04:38 - Maya Chen: sure. the pilot success criteria as i have them: 1) p95 latency <200ms and p99 <350ms on production-like load; 2) per-request cost reduction vs your current provider by at least 25% after caching and batching; 3) classification/regression delta <1.5% vs baseline; 4) security sign-offs (SOC2 artifacts, SAML, KMS) and network connectivity validated; 5) ops runbook and monitoring integrated with your dashboards. anyone disagree?
05:05 - Vikram Shah: looks good, just add throughput floor — we need sustained 150 qps with occasional spikes to 250 qps.
05:13 - Maya Chen: good call — adding throughput floor: sustain 150 qps with bursts to 250 qps for 10 minutes.
05:20 - Rita Gomez: also add deployment window and budget approval as gating items — we won't move to dedicated until finance signs SOW.
05:27 - Maya Chen: noted.
05:30 - Alex Park: on the dataset side, vikram will share a final 7 day anonymized log set for the final benchmark. are there any format constraints?
05:38 - Samir Patel: CSV or parquet fine, hashed user ids, no PII. ideally we get a small schema mapping doc. if you want we can provide a simple ingestion script.
05:47 - Vikram Shah: we'll provide parquet with schema v1.2 and a short mapping. aim to send by 2025-10-09.
05:54 - Samir Patel: great. i'll run the bench once it's in. i'll also turn on KV cache and the quantized path for the run, and try the larger batch window.
06:05 - Tom Nguyen: on connectivity, we'll need the redwood IP ranges and a short list of ports. also do you support private link / transit gateway?
06:14 - Samir Patel: yes, we support VPC peering and peered transit. i'll include the network doc. private link availability depends on region — i'll confirm for your region.
06:26 - Lena Ortiz: any blockers from your side, rita?
06:29 - Rita Gomez: none immediate. i just want the exec review in place; finance will want a clear TCO with committed vs on-demand comparisons.
06:38 - Maya Chen: understood. we'll provide a TCO sheet that compares hosted, dedicated, and private options with an assumed 12 month commit.
06:47 - Alex Park: what's the proposed timeline to close the pilot?
06:50 - Maya Chen: if we get logs by 10/09 and run a 72-hour benchmark starting 10/10, we can have results by 10/15, then a week for internal review — so exec sign-off by 10/22 is realistic.
07:05 - Rita Gomez: that timeline works.
07:08 - Samir Patel: technical note — during the benchmark i'll capture token-level cost, per-route latency, and top N failure modes. we'll share a spreadsheet and a quick walkthrough. also we'll include the model variant names we used — there was a little transcription error earlier where the model alias printed as "rw-infer-v2" but in some logs it appeared as "redwood-inf"; we'll normalize naming in the report.
07:33 - Vikram Shah: good to know. on monitoring — can we get token-level metrics exported to our datadog account?
07:39 - Samir Patel: yes, we have datadog integrations and you can pull per-route metrics. we also support Prometheus pull for internal infra.
07:48 - Lena Ortiz: anything else for risks?
07:50 - Tom Nguyen: firewall and peering timing, and potential SSO onboarding delays.
07:54 - Maya Chen: ok wrap up — quick recap of decisions and owners.
08:00 - Maya Chen: decisions: run final 72 hour benchmark with KV + quant + larger batch on dedicated-like config; success criteria as read back; security packet to be sent; Redwood to provide network doc and pricing/SOW.
08:14 - Action items read quickly: maya to send pricing & SOW 10/10, samir to run latency runs and bench 10/08-10/15, vikram to provide logs 10/09, tom to confirm VPC details 10/07, rita to schedule exec sign-off by 10/15.
08:33 - Alex Park: thanks all.
08:35 - Maya Chen: thanks — i'll follow up with calendar invites for the exec review and share the packet. bye.
08:39 - Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts (model alias, "KV cache" spacing, minor name spellings). References shared: security_packet_link (will be attached in follow-up), pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx (to be sent), benchmark_results_template.csv (redwood).
